gates.description: The item concerns materials/polymer R&D, lab automation, manufacturing or recycling data, or presents a method whose transfer to materials R&D can be explained concretely (name the mechanism, not just 'could apply to materials'). Generic model launches, leaderboards, funding, finance, policy and front-end/software news fail unless the item itself reports a concrete R&D link.
The item adds a new fact, method, result, dataset, tool release or substantive analysis. Re-reports, roundups, opinion without new evidence and announcements without technical content fail.

The core claims can be traced to an original source (paper, preprint, code, dataset, technical report, first-party engineering write-up). Pure marketing, unattributed claims and reposts that do not identify the original fail.

dimensions.description: How directly it helps materials R&D decisions: formulation, experiment design, property prediction, data context (batch, processing history, equipment, test conditions, provenance), robustness across batches/equipment/suppliers, uncertainty and failure detection, lab automation, process control, defect detection, sorting/recycling.

Strength of evidence available in what was supplied, judged by content type: papers need materials/data scale, baselines and validation (held-out, cross-batch, experimental confirmation); industrial cases need named site/line, before-after metrics and period; tools need runnable code, docs and examples. Abstract-only access caps this at 6 unless the abstract itself reports baselines and validation.
Whether the method can be carried to other materials, processes or labs, and how clearly the transfer conditions (data needs, instrumentation, assumptions) are stated.

Closeness to industrial use: scale, real process data, cost/throughput/yield/cycle-time/stability constraints actually reported. Do not infer cost, carbon or yield effects that the item does not report.
Information gain over well-known prior work or earlier coverage of the same work.
